subject: Post-call workback: HealBridge feature finability & payback
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Liana Cheng <liana@healbridge.com>, Michael Tan <mtan@healbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + workback items (feature-level econ)

Thanks again for taking the call today — good discussion on where HealBridge wants to position the two features (Clinical Assist and Member Q&A) and the target payback window. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can turn this into a short workback for procurement/internal finance.

Summary notes:
- Scope: two distinct features: Clinical Assist (high-sensitivity suggestions, ~25M tokens/mo expected) and Member Q&A (short, high-volume → ~10M tokens/mo).
- Target commercial goals you mentioned: maintain >55% gross margin on feature-level P&L and CAC payback within 6–9 months for the initial pilot cohort.
- Rough budget band you shared on the call: $30k–$70k/mo total inference budget depending on conversion assumptions and volume.

Immediate asks (to unblock a pricing sketch):
1) Confirm expected monthly tokens by endpoint (we have the 25M / 10M split as above — please confirm).
2) Share a representative sample request/response (anonymized) for both features — we can run a quick token histogram. I attached example-payloads.json to show the format we prefer.
3) Tell us target CAC per paid user (or range) so we can do the payback math. You mentioned ~ $35–$60 in acquisition today — confirm.

What Redwood will provide in the next email: a short, scenario-based unit-econ workback showing: effective $/1M tokens under (a) hosted baseline, (b) committed monthly reservation, (c) quantized model path; then per-feature $/feature and months-to-payback given your CAC and revenue per user inputs.

Attachments: healbridge-econ-workback.csv (blank template) — please fill tokens by endpoint + expected MAU.

Next steps / timeline:
- Liana: confirm token split + CAC by Fri 4/23.
- Sean: deliver workback scenarios by Mon 4/26.

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Cc: Michael Tan <mtan@healbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + workback items (feature-level econ)

Thanks Sean — quick confirmations and a few clarifying Qs.

Confirmed:
- Token split looks right to us: Clinical Assist ~25M/mo, Member Q&A ~10M/mo (these are pilot targets — can scale).
- CAC: our current paid-user CAC range is $40–$55 (we acquire via channel partners; want to see payback <= 9 months ideally, 6 months preferred).

Questions:
1) For the $/1M tokens scenarios, can you show both our retailable $/feature (what we need to charge customers) and Redwood's effective cost (what we would pay you) so we can map margins?
2) We likely need SOC2 evidence for procurement — who on your side handles that? (CC'd Ben for procurement pipeline.)

I attached a short note (healbridge_internal_assumptions.xlsx) with our MAU breakdown and our conservative ARPU estimate by feature. If you need anything else, call out line items and we can respond.

Liana
Director, Product — HealBridge
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Liana Cheng <liana@healbridge.com>, Michael Tan <mtan@healbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-24T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + workback items (feature-level econ) — draft scenarios attached

Appended a short, conservative workback based on your inputs — see attached redwood-pricing-scenarios.xlsx and the CSV template populated (healbridge-econ-workback.csv). Below is the tl;dr with three scenarios and per-feature outcomes so you can react quickly.

Assumptions used (from your input + Redwood defaults):
- Token split: Clinical Assist = 25M/mo, Member Q&A = 10M/mo.
- CAC used for payback calc = $48 (midpoint of your range).
- Revenue per new paid user attributable to feature: Clinical Assist = $9/mo, Member Q&A = $3.50/mo (from your ARPU sheet).
- Redwood effective cost (hosted):
  • Hosted baseline (no commit, default optimizations): $28 / 1M tokens
  • Committed reservation (6–12mo commit, modest discount): $18 / 1M tokens
  • Aggressive quantized/edge variant (specialized model + reserved infra): $12 / 1M tokens

Scenario calculations (monthly):
- Clinical Assist (25M tokens):
  • Cost @ $28/1M = 25 * $28 = $700
  • Cost @ $18/1M = 25 * $18 = $450
  • Cost @ $12/1M = 25 * $12 = $300
- Member Q&A (10M tokens):
  • Cost @ $28/1M = 10 * $28 = $280
  • Cost @ $18/1M = 10 * $18 = $180
  • Cost @ $12/1M = 10 * $12 = $120

Per-feature $/feature (unit-level view):
- Clinical Assist: tokens per MAU = 500, MAU assumed 50k (pilot), tokens -> 25M. If revenue per MAU = $9/mo, gross revenue = 50k * $9 = $450k/mo.
  • Inference cost share (committed $18/1M) = $450/mo.
  • % of revenue = $450 / $450,000 = 0.1% (negligible in pilot due to scale of ARPU).
  • Margin impact: with $18/1M, inference is not the main cost — margin stays >99% before CAC.
- Member Q&A: MAU 100k (larger reach), ARPU $3.50 -> revenue = 350k/mo, cost @ $18/1M = $180/mo -> 0.05% of revenue.

CAC payback implications (simplified):
- Using CAC = $48 and incremental gross margin after inference only: both features show very fast payback on inference alone because inference cost per new user is tiny at these ARPU numbers; the dominant payback driver will be net revenue per user after product costs (support, infra beyond inference).
- Example (Clinical Assist): incremental margin per new user = $9/mo (revenue) - negligible incremental inference (~$0.009 per user at $18/1M) ~= $9/mo. Payback on $48 CAC = $48 / $9 = 5.3 months.

Key takeaways / what this means for pricing negotiation:
1) At the MAU and ARPU numbers you shared, inference cost is a very small fraction of feature-level revenue — even at hosted baseline rates. That gives you lots of flexibility on list price.
2) The lever that matters: committed reservation + quantized variants (move from $28 -> $12–18 per 1M) mainly reduces vendor cost volatility and gives predictable unit economics for planning.
3) If you expect ARPU to be materially lower for certain cohorts, the $/1M token bands above are the sensitivity to watch.

Proposed next steps (pick one):
A) Procurement: we can draft a short reserved capacity commercial to get you to the $18/1M band (6–12 month term). Ben — can you start a procurement thread and share the SOC2 link?
B) Technical: we run token histograms on the sample payloads to validate the 500 tokens/MAU assumption and identify batching opportunities (Marissa, can you own this?).
C) Pilot offer: 30-day reserved pilot at a mid-point price ($18/1M) + 2-week performance validation.

If that all looks reasonable I can draft a short one-pager that maps scenarios to list prices and margin outcomes for your CFO.

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

This is very helpful — thanks for the clear scenarios. Two quick asks before we share with finance:
1) Can you convert the per-user inference cost into a $/feature metric at the cohort level (new paid cohort of 5k users)? We want to show execs the incremental line-item.
2) Please include the SOC2 evidence link and a sample contract term showing commit length vs discount.

Ben — looping you to start procurement cadence. Sean/Marissa — if you can send the cohort-level CSV (example attached) we’ll schedule a quick pricing review with our CFO on 4/30.

Liana
